clue.text: Cargo in spillage was not chemical fertiliser

definitions.note: an adjective describing manure-type feed for crops made without synthetic chemicals

indicators.note: a spillage scatters a load everywhere, so the letters of the two words before it are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cargo of fertiliser spilt, and an inspector reports it was not the chemical kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: CARGO IN is rearranged, signalled by 'spillage'. 'was' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming described this way uses natural manures and composts instead of synthetic chemical feeds.

clue.text: Support platform out of the audience's view

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a stage is a raised platform for performers

explanation.surface: A supporting platform is hidden from the theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The area behind the scenery and wings of a theatre is unseen by those watching the show.

parts.note: the devil's ___ is an old phrase for idly drumming the fingers, and the same word names an evening military pageant with bands

explanation.surface: A question about what parade Satan's army would put on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'devil's tattoo' is a restless drumming of fingers on a table; on its own the word is also a military display such as the Edinburgh one, a famous Scottish event with massed bands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an outdoor military pageant of drumming and marching, and completes the old idiom for nervous finger-drumming.

parts.note: reads as the way a household is run, but means a region's right to govern its own affairs, a term from Irish politics

explanation.surface: A question about who is in charge around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' suggests the household; the phrase is the political term for a region running its own internal affairs, famous from the Irish campaign for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the political term for devolved government of a country's internal affairs, literally rule at house level.

parts.note: sounds like a race with a narrow margin, but means combat at arm's length, body against body

explanation.surface: A neck-and-neck race or election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' wants to mean narrowly decided; it means physically close, a fight at grappling range.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat at grappling range, without weapons fired from a distance, is as physically close as a contest gets.

clue.text: Frenchman cooked risotto for one at the wheel

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French title for a man

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French chef made risotto for a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: M for Monsieur is a crossword convention; 'cooked' is the anagram signal, so the Frenchman is not the cook but a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver of a car sits at the steering wheel.

definitions.meaning: describing something circular or turning about a centre
a song sung by several voices entering in turn with the same tune, like Frère Jacques

explanation.definitionFit: Circular shapes revolve, and a canon such as Frère Jacques is a song sung in overlapping turns.

clue.text: Almost permit two articles being forgetful

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for permit is dropped

parts.note: to let is to permit
the is the definite article
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone nearly allows two items to slip their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts LET to LE; 'two articles' gives both THE and AN. Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the river Lethe made the dead lose all memory, so its adjective means causing oblivion.

indicators.note: surrounds means the word for artillery goes around the word for frantic

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
mad means frantic or frenzied

explanation.surface: A gun battery encircles a panicking fleet of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic fleet' reads as a description, but 'frantic' supplies its own word; RA (Royal Artillery) is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a large fleet of warships, as with the Spanish one of 1588.

indicators.note: outside means the word for letter goes round the word for leave

parts.note: a note is a short letter
to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone almost leaves the letter outside the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave letter outside' reads as an instruction about post; 'outside' is the container signal, with the letter on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means almost but falling just short.

parts.note: covered in a short coat, as a potato is baked in its skin

explanation.surface: A question about something given a quick coat of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' suggests briefly; it is a short coat, the garment worn over a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A short coat worn on the upper body gives the word for being covered in one.

parts.note: sounds like a strict mentor, but is the steering blade at the rear of a boat

explanation.surface: A strict mentor or tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' reads as strict; it is the back of a ship, where the steering blade hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged blade at the back of a vessel steers it.

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer was also struck down by a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges VIRUS TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly skilled performer, especially an instrumentalist, is called this.

indicators.note: out of signals the letters coming out of order, a rearrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone rushes in out of the sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges SUNLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustling about at speed is to hurry or rush.

parts.note: hanging about with intent to commit a crime was an offence under an old English vagrancy law

explanation.surface: Acting illegally and on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with intent' completes the British legal phrase for lurking about with criminal intention, an offence under the Vagrancy Act of 1824.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingering about with criminal purpose was a crime known by the phrase ending 'with intent'.

clue.text: It is also akin, somehow, to a Greek city

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that something is also related to a city in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges ALSO AKIN; 'It is' and 'to' just link. It is an older name of Thessaloniki.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older English name for Thessaloniki, the second city of Greece.

clue.text: Tell someone to move out of the way of course?

definitions.text: Tell someone to move out of the way of course?

parts.words: Tell someone to move out of the way of course?
parts.note: a golfer shouts a warning to people on the course in the path of the ball, which also means to caution in advance

explanation.surface: Asking someone to shift aside, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as naturally; it is a golf course, where 'Fore!' is shouted to warn people in the line of the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution someone in advance is to alert them, and on a golf course the cry 'Fore!' gives such an alert.

clue.text: Very best work is by Timothy, a student

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: The finest piece of work is one by a student called Timothy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is by' just links; L for a learner is from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: The most favourable or best possible outcome is described this way.

parts.note: kin is family, with the possessive s
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A family's man is a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags that the wordplay, read straight, is itself a fair description: KIN'S plus MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A male member of one's family or blood relation.

clue.text: Join together neatly at back of bird?

definitions.meaning: to fit closely together, like interlocking wood joints
the hind end of a pigeon-like bird, a fanciful reading

explanation.definitionFit: A wood joint with wedge-shaped interlocking pieces fits neatly together, and literally the rear end of a pigeon-like bird.

clue.text: Sailor during first half of trip became devoted adherent

indicators.note: during means the sailor comes in the middle of the trip's letters
first half of keeps only the opening three letters of the six-letter word for trip

parts.note: a voyage is a trip
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman became a devoted follower halfway through a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' trims the six-letter word for trip to its first three letters, and 'during' puts the sailor inside; 'became' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee or ardent follower of a cause or religion, originally one bound by vows.

clue.text: Cut back in southern firm's plaster

indicators.note: in means the reversed word goes inside the letters for southern and firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: back means the word cut is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Cuts are made to a southern company's plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the word cut round to TUC, and 'in' sets it between the southern and firm letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine plaster or cement coating for walls and mouldings.

clue.text: Gaming-table attendant ie right to leave with a cough

indicators.note: to leave means the letters for ie and right depart from the attendant's title

parts.note: a croupier runs a casino gaming table
ie as written

explanation.surface: A casino dealer is permitted to leave because of a cough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes IE and R from the end of CROUPIER; 'with' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflammation of a child's windpipe causing a harsh barking cough.

indicators.note: repair means fix by rearranging, so the letters of the two words before it are reordered

explanation.surface: Worry about the roadworks in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' rearranges IN STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a stake or share in something, as a business holding.

parts.note: reads as demanding, but means levying a tax, putting a duty upon something

explanation.surface: A one-word question about something demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxing' wants to mean arduous; it means levying, as a duty is laid on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy a tax is to lay a charge on people or goods.

parts.note: a letter here is one who lets property, and the money from tenants is what they receive

explanation.surface: Money arriving in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' wants to be correspondence; it is someone who lets out property, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: The money paid by tenants is what a landlord, one who lets, collects.

clue.text: Turn over half the underwear perhaps being disrespectful

parts.note: to flip is to turn over
pants come as a pair, so half of them would whimsically be a single one

explanation.surface: Someone turns over half the underwear rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants are a plural pair, so a single leg of them, 'half the underwear', is one PANT; 'perhaps' admits it is a whimsical picture. 'being' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means lacking proper seriousness, treating a matter lightly or with disrespect.
